chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants in His decree and judgment, but He is Just in that.
And He is not unjust in His decree, but the servant is unjust to himself by abandoning obedience and committing sin.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology explain Divine Justice if Allah decrees all things?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) elucidation of the Shia doctrine of Divine Justice (*Adl*), refuting the Qadariyyah and Mu'tazilah extremes by affirming that Allah’s decree is inherently just. The Imam clarifies that apparent 'injustice' in human experience stems not from God, but from the servant’s own volition to abandon obedience or commit sin, thereby making them the author of their own detriment. This hadith serves as a foundational proof for the principle that divine recompense is always proportional to human free will and choice.
